# dsh-bundles
English | 中文
**One-click, persona-based plugin bundles for DeepSeek Harness.** Choose how you work, review the in
cluded community plugins, and install the complete toolkit from one card.
Website · Plugin market · Bundle catalog

Successful installs write an ownership ledger to `.dsh-bundles/state.json` in the target profile. Un
install removes only packages installed exclusively by that bundle; pre-existing packages and packag
es still referenced by another bundle are preserved. Use `list` and `status [bundle-id]` to inspect
installation and management state. Legacy adoption requires explicit confirmation and claims package
s without another ownership record; it never happens automatically, so independently installed packa
ges are not silently made removable.
For source testing before a release, use `dsh plugin --profile web add --allow-build=dshbundles gith
ub:LM20230311/dsh-bundles#main`.
## Use a bundle

1. Click anywhere on a persona card to expand its plugin list.
2. Click a plugin row to inspect its

description, source, repository, and market metadata.
3. Click **Install all** to install the comple
te bundle and watch live progress; afterwards, use **Safe uninstall** from the same card. For a comp
lete legacy install, use **Manage legacy install** first.
Already-installed plugins are skipped. Before changing the profile, dsh-bundles snapshots `package.j
son` and `pnpm-lock.yaml`; if a required plugin fails, it restores the previous dependency state.
Each pnpm command has a three-minute default deadline. A timeout terminates the complete process gro
up and enters the existing rollback path instead of leaving the UI stuck on “installing”. Set `DSHBU
NDLES_PNPM_TIMEOUT_MS` to override the deadline in milliseconds on slower networks.
## What you get
| Capability | Details |
| Persona bundles | 6 curated toolkits and 29 community plugins for developers, creators, designers,

students, researchers, and fun |
| One-click workflow | Full-card expansion, bundle preview, one-cl

ick install, safe uninstall, live progress, and per-plugin results |
| Plugin details | Install sour
ce and repository links for every catalog entry; richer descriptions, author, downloads, stars, cate

gories, and screenshots when dshmarket is installed |
| Safe recovery | Skips installed packages, pr

eserves pre-existing/shared plugins, and rolls back failed install or uninstall operations |

## dshmarket integration
dshmarket is optional. Install it directly from the bundle page, then use localized dshmarket detail
links to inspect, update, or remove individual plugins. Remote community bundles are accepted only
when every npm package is present in dshmarket's curated registry.
## Submit a bundle
Publish a community bundle at dshbundles.com/publish. The site validates every package against dshma
rket's curated registry and exposes verified bundles to the same catalog consumed inside DSH.
To propose or update an official built-in bundle:

1. Edit `data/bundles.json`.
2. Give every bundle a unique `id`, localized `persona` and `tagline`,

and at least one plugin.
3. Use `target` for GitHub or tarball installation sources when the plugin

name is not directly installable.
4. Run `npm run check`, then open a pull request.
## Development
[代码示例省略，未执行]
`npm run check` runs both TypeScript projects, the installer/route tests, and the client bundle buil
d. `npm run audit:bundles` checks npm availability, DSH manifests, release activity, and weekly down
load signals for every official plugin, then updates `reports/bundle-audit.md`.
